summary: MQTT (1883/tcp, 8883/tcp TLS) has ZERO coverage in recce today — the port is not in `svcdetect.PORT_NAMES`, not in `serviceenum._NAME` or `_PORT`, has no signature in `_SIGNATURES`, and no `recce/services/mqtt.py` module exists. An open MQTT broker leaks topic namespace, retained messages, WILL credentials, and often the ClientID roster — a very high-signal cross-service surface (hostnames, usernames, hashes). Build shape mirrors `services/kafka.py`: length-prefixed binary framing + a bounded probe function returning a dict, plus `analyze()` + `findings()` + `runbook()`. Reference: OASIS mqtt-v3.1.1-os (§3.1 CONNECT, §3.2 CONNACK, §3.3 PUBLISH incl. RETAIN, §3.8 SUBSCRIBE) and OASIS mqtt-v5.0 (§3.1 Properties, §3.14 DISCONNECT reason codes). MQTT-SN (UDP 1884) is out of scope for tranche 1.
default_ports: 80/tcp + 443/tcp with WebSockets subprotocol 'mqtt' (out of scope for tranche 1 — covered by web enum if surfaced)

existing_coverage.notes: No hits for 'mqtt', 1883, or 8883 anywhere under recce/ (excluding node_modules). PORT_NAMES in svcdetect.py has no MQTT entry so port 1883 with an unhelpful nmap label falls through to 'unknown'; _SIGNATURES has no 0x10/0x20 CONNECT/CONNACK matcher; serviceenum._NAME and _PORT have no mqtt entry so `recce services` prints nothing actionable next to an MQTT port; no per-service script maps to it.

capabilities.name: port-inference
capabilities.description: Add 1883 -> ('mqtt', 'MQTT broker (plaintext, OASIS 3.1.1/v5)') and 8883 -> ('mqtts', 'MQTT broker (TLS)') to svcdetect.PORT_NAMES so an unlabelled port gets an inferred label with zero traffic. Also add 1884/tcp (Mosquitto WSS convention) as a soft hint.

capabilities.name: connack-signature
capabilities.description: Add a byte-signature to svcdetect._SIGNATURES matching a CONNACK reply (fixed header 0x20 0x02 + 2 flag/reason bytes) so a stray high-port MQTT broker that answered a CONNECT nudge (or leaked a mid-session PUBLISH starting 0x30) is auto-labelled 'mqtt' from banner bytes rather than staying 'unknown'. Complements grab_banner's HTTP fallback — MQTT stays mute until a CONNECT is sent, so a dedicated nudge (see next capability) is what actually makes this fire.

capabilities.name: connect-nudge
capabilities.description: In svcdetect._NUDGE (or an MQTT-specific branch) send a minimal MQTT 3.1.1 CONNECT for port 1883 (fixed header 0x10 + remaining-length + protocol name 'MQTT' + level 0x04 + clean-session + keepalive + empty ClientID). Read the CONNACK, then the reason code (byte 3) already tells us auth policy: 0x00 = anonymous accepted; 0x02 = 'identifier rejected' (still a broker, empty ClientID banned); 0x04 = bad user/password (auth required); 0x05 = not authorised. Zero credentials sent; result is a per-port policy fingerprint feeding the finding gate.
capabilities.protocol_reference: OASIS mqtt-v3.1.1-os §3.1 CONNECT, §3.2 CONNACK (Table 3.1 return codes)

capabilities.name: anonymous-connect
capabilities.description: Full-fat probe of an anonymous CONNECT with an auto-generated ClientID ('recce-' + 6 hex). CONNACK 0x00 without username/password is the headline HIGH finding — a public write/read broker. Record broker's granted keepalive, session-present bit, and (v5) any Server Reference / Server Keep Alive / Maximum QoS properties.
capabilities.protocol_reference: OASIS mqtt-v3.1.1-os §3.1.2.3 Clean Session, §3.2.2 CONNACK; OASIS mqtt-v5.0 §3.1.2.11 CONNECT Properties, §3.2.2.3 CONNACK Properties

capabilities.name: empty-clientid-accepted
capabilities.description: MQTT 3.1.1 §3.1.3.1 lets a broker accept an empty ClientID only when CleanSession=1; many brokers silently accept it under any config. Send CONNECT with ClientID length=0. CONNACK 0x00 = broker allows anonymous session with no identity at all (HIGH — anti-forensic; concurrent 'ghost' clients cannot be told apart, and other clients using empty ClientID get their sessions stolen).

capabilities.name: protocol-version-probe
capabilities.description: Send both CONNECT v3.1.1 (level 0x04) and CONNECT v5 (level 0x05); a v5 broker returns extra properties in CONNACK (Assigned Client Identifier, Server Keep Alive, Maximum Packet Size, Retain Available, Wildcard Subscription Available, Shared Subscription Available, Server Reference). Parse them — 'Retain Available=1' + 'Wildcard Subscription Available=1' are what makes the retained-message exfil below realistic. Also record which versions the broker refuses (CONNACK 0x01 = unacceptable protocol version) as a fingerprint.

capabilities.name: wildcard-subscribe-hash
capabilities.description: After a successful anonymous CONNECT, SUBSCRIBE to '#' (root multi-level wildcard) at QoS 0 for a bounded window (~2-3s). RETAIN-flagged PUBLISH packets arrive immediately — the broker replays every retained message on every topic. Record topic tree + payload sizes + a per-topic sample (truncated) for the report. Retained messages routinely contain device state, credentials, JWTs, plaintext config. CRITICAL finding when >0 retained messages leak; HIGH when only live traffic leaks. Cap payload capture (e.g. 256 bytes/topic, 200 topics) to keep the probe bounded — sensitive data goes to the loot dir, not the sheet.
capabilities.protocol_reference: OASIS mqtt-v3.1.1-os §4.7 Topic Names and Topic Filters (# multi-level wildcard), §3.3.1.3 RETAIN

capabilities.name: sys-topic-scrape
capabilities.description: Subscribe to '$SYS/#' (Mosquitto/HiveMQ convention) — broker version, uptime, client count, bytes sent/received, live client-list on some brokers. Highest signal: '$SYS/broker/version' pins vendor+version straight into port.product/port.version (feeds CVE map — Mosquitto <2.0.15, EMQX <5.0.9, HiveMQ CE, etc). Distinct from '#' because $SYS is often filtered from '#' by broker policy but readable directly.
capabilities.protocol_reference: Mosquitto broker docs — $SYS topic hierarchy (de-facto standard, no OASIS spec)

capabilities.name: publish-permission-test
capabilities.description: PUBLISH a tiny benign marker ('recce-probe-<uuid>') at QoS 1 to a canary topic ('recce/probe/<uuid>'), then SUBSCRIBE and confirm receipt. Success = broker accepts anonymous WRITE (CRITICAL — the broker is a public bus, attacker can inject commands to any subscribing device: home automation, industrial controls, telemetry corruption). Clean up: PUBLISH empty retained message to the same topic to clear it. Skip when broker returned SUBACK with rejected QoS (0x80) on '#' — write is very likely also gated.

capabilities.name: credential-spray
capabilities.description: Bounded CONNECT sweep with (creds.known_users x tiny weak-password list: '', <user>, mqtt, admin, password, changeme, 1883). Small — MQTT has no lockout in the spec and brokers rarely rate-limit, but keep it to N*M<=40 and single-target-serial to avoid DoS. CONNACK 0x00 = valid cred; record to shared cred store. Complements wildcard-subscribe: an auth-gated broker becomes a full retained-message dump once one cred hits.
capabilities.protocol_reference: OASIS mqtt-v3.1.1-os §3.1.2.8/9 UserName/Password flags, §3.2.2 CONNACK 0x04/0x05 reason codes

capabilities.name: will-message-inspection
capabilities.description: MQTT lets a client register a Last-Will PUBLISH the broker sends on ungraceful disconnect. Some brokers expose current wills via $SYS or make them observable when we forcibly disconnect a subscribed session. Additionally, a subscribe to '#' catches wills as they fire in real time (see wildcard-subscribe-hash). Wills routinely include device identity + tokens ('device/42/status offline, token=eyJ...'). Report distinctly because they identify device roster and often carry secrets.

capabilities.name: banner-version-fingerprint
capabilities.description: Pin broker product/version from three complementary sources: (a) CONNACK v5 property 0x1F 'Reason String' on rejection (often names broker), (b) $SYS/broker/version (see sys-topic-scrape), (c) Mosquitto 2.x quirk of returning ProtocolError on malformed CONNECT with a distinctive length-prefix. Write into port.product / port.version so recce's CVE mapper picks it up (Mosquitto: CVE-2023-28366 memory leak, CVE-2023-3592 use-after-free; EMQX: CVE-2024-43201 auth bypass; HiveMQ: CVE-2023-33461).

capabilities.name: tls-alpn-and-cert
capabilities.description: For port 8883 (and any other port whose CONNACK arrived over TLS), use the existing tls probe path: capture cert SANs (feeds core.known_hostnames — MQTT brokers are commonly issued certs with the internal hostname), verify chain, note weak ciphers / expired certs / self-signed. Record ALPN — spec says MQTT-over-TLS does NOT use ALPN, so a broker advertising 'mqtt' ALPN is uncommon but noteworthy.
capabilities.protocol_reference: OASIS mqtt-v3.1.1-os §5.4 Network Connections; IANA ALPN registry ('mqtt' is registered for WebSocket subprotocol only)

capabilities.name: topic-namespace-loot
capabilities.description: Persist the observed topic tree to loot/mqtt/<ip>-<port>-topics.txt and feed distinctive path segments cross-service: 'homeassistant/*/config', 'zigbee2mqtt/*', 'shellies/*', 'tele/*' -> device fingerprints; 'devices/<hostname>/*' -> known_hostnames candidates; 'users/<name>/*' -> known_users candidates. Downstream: web enum uses hostnames when re-scanning HTTP/HTTPS; kerberos/ldap enum uses usernames.

capabilities.name: auth-required-info-finding
capabilities.description: Symmetric with kafka_saslgated: when TCP connects and CONNECT is answered by CONNACK 0x04/0x05 (or the socket is torn down mid-handshake), emit a low/info 'mqtt_authgated' finding recording the reason code + broker version if extractable. Marks the endpoint as a target for any looted MQTT/IoT credential and confirms auth is actually enforced (vs the port merely being firewalled at connect).

cross_service_wire_candidates: known_hostnames — TLS cert SANs on 8883 (existing probes.py cert code), plus device hostnames mined from topic path segments like 'devices/<host>/*', 'homeassistant/<host>/*', 'zigbee2mqtt/<host>/*', $SYS/broker/uptime replies

known_users — ClientIDs harvested from live PUBLISH source (v5 assigned-client-identifier property, retained payloads containing 'user'/'client', '$SYS/broker/clients' lists on Mosquitto). MQTT ClientIDs are frequently reused as usernames on other services (device identity), and Will Message payloads often include 'user=' fields

known_hashes — Retained PUBLISH payloads regularly contain JWTs, API tokens, bcrypt hashes (broker used as a config bus). Scan captured payloads for the same patterns hashloot uses; feed matches to the shared hash store
known_domains — TLS cert issuer/subject on 8883, plus MQTT broker $SYS/broker/version strings that embed a hostname ('mosquitto version 2.0.15 running on broker.internal.corp')
relay_targets — an anonymous-writable broker is a lateral-movement staging point (publish a command to any subscribing device); record as 'mqtt-write' relay for the attack-path graph

NEW: known_topics — a first-class cross-service surface. Distinct from all existing wires because topic paths carry structure (namespace/device/action) other IoT-adjacent scanners could seed against — Modbus/OPC-UA scans, HTTP api enum ('/api/mqtt/topics'), Kafka topic-name correlation (same names used on both bus systems in mixed IoT-cloud stacks)
NEW: known_devices — device fingerprints (mqtt vendor conventions: shelly, tasmota, zigbee2mqtt, wled, esphome, hass) feed a shared IoT device roster consumed by upnp, ssdp, coap, mdns (post-tranche)
port.product / port.version — direct feed into recce's CVE mapper (per _fill_product path in svcdetect) for Mosquitto/EMQX/HiveMQ/VerneMQ CVEs

recommended_findings.title: MQTT broker leaks retained messages on wildcard subscribe (#)
MQTT broker leaks $SYS metrics (version, clients, uptime)
MQTT broker accepts anonymous PUBLISH (public write bus)
MQTT broker accepts empty ClientID (ghost/session-hijack risk)
MQTT credential accepted via low-effort spray (weak/default password)
MQTT Will Message discloses device identity/token
MQTT broker on 1883/tcp without TLS (plaintext credentials on the wire)
MQTT broker running end-of-life / known-CVE version

implementation_notes: Build `recce/services/mqtt.py` mirroring `services/kafka.py` shape: stdlib socket + struct only, bounded probe, `is_mqtt(port)` + `mqtt_targets(hosts)` + `probe(ip, port, timeout)` returning `{reachable, version, anon_ok, empty_clientid_ok, publish_ok, sys, retained: [{topic, size, snippet}], live: [...], reason, error}` + `findings(hosts, probes)` + `runbook(ip, port)` + `analyze(hosts, creds, active, budget, progress)`. MQTT framing: fixed header byte 1 = packet-type<<4 | flags, then variable-length remaining-length (1-4 bytes, 7-bit continuation like protobuf varint — implement `_encode_remlen`/`_decode_remlen`). Packet types: CONNECT=1, CONNACK=2, PUBLISH=3, PUBACK=4, SUBSCRIBE=8, SUBACK=9, UNSUBSCRIBE=10, DISCONNECT=14. Strings are length-prefixed UTF-8 (uint16 length). For v5 add a Properties section (varint length + typed fields). Wire into `svcdetect.PORT_NAMES` (1883, 8883, 1884) + `_SIGNATURES` (CONNACK 0x20 0x02); wire into `serviceenum._NAME` ('mqtt', 'mqtts', 'secure-mqtt') and `_PORT` (1883, 8883); add `mqtt` to `scripts/recce-service.sh` name_to_svc/port_to_svc so `recce services` prints an actionable next command (`mosquitto_sub -h {ip} -p {port} -t '#' -v -W 3` for anon, `mosquitto_sub -h {ip} -p {port} -u <user> -P <pass> -t '$SYS/#'` for auth). Retained-payload capture writes to loot/mqtt/<ip>-<port>/ (out-of-sheet — sensitive). Every probe uses `svcprobe.iter_probe` for budget/progress consistent with other services. Cleanup after `publish-permission-test` is mandatory (empty retained publish to zero the canary). All active probes must respect `active=False` for passive-only runs.
